accounting.rationale: Both sentences define the statement-to-SAVE route. Listed entities receive the canonical8.5.16 attribute; an omitted list is treated as the names of all allowed items in the same scoping unit. Eligibility, retained states, COMMON obligations, execution events and pointer/host lifetimes remain with their original owners. This is not another local S/runtime classifier.
The first sentence applies to the list-bearing form, not the separate bare-SAVE interpretation.
The attribute is8.5.16 SAVE. Specifying it does not initialize an undefined variable, establish pointer association, allocate an object or promise physical static storage.
Every listed entity retains its resolved data/procedure-pointer/common-block role and C861/C862 eligibility. A COMMON block is distinct from its members.
The second sentence concerns omission of the entire saved-entity-list group. SAVE :: without a list is not an independently licensed bare form.

All is qualified by allowed. Dummy arguments, function results, automatic data objects, individual COMMON members and named constants are not made SAVE-eligible by omitting the list;8.3/C814 and8.5.16/C861/C862 retain their owners.

The scope is not an inclusive scope, every program unit or all storage reachable through saved pointers.3.120,11.1.4/C1108,19.4 and19.5.1.4 determine nested/BLOCK/local/host identities; module/main/submodule implicit SAVE has its separate8.5.16p4 route.
The original SAVE A,B,C,/BLOCKA/,D illustrates a mixed list only. It provides no complete declarations, program, processor observation or new normative effect.
This is an example of the list-bearing form without double colons, not an additional requirement.
The ordinary names must resolve to allowed saved entities in any complete future context; their spelling does not establish type, initialization or eligibility.
The paired slashes identify named block BLOCKA, not a COMMON member or blank common. Full declarations and cross-scope COMMON/SAVE conditions remain necessary.
Do not turn the fragment into a no-op effect, assume missing declarations, or duplicate an existing COMMON retention/control program.

requirements.title: SAVE permits a qualified entity list or an omitted-list form
requirements.source: 8.6.14 R859, J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF140, printed126.
requirements.definition: The SAVE keyword may stand alone or be followed by a nonempty saved-entity list, optionally preceded by ::. The separator is inside the list-bearing optional group and is not a listless alternative. R401/R860 supply the list and its entity alternatives; C893 and the canonical eligibility/scope rules remain active. Paragraph1 defines how the two statement forms specify the existing SAVE attribute.

pending.listed-double-colon-form: PENDING compile/positive-control admission in a complete ordinary non-PURE subroutine: INTEGER :: kept followed by one SAVE :: kept. There is no declaration initializer, DATA, other SAVE route, dummy/result/automatic role or payload read. A module/main implicit-SAVE confirmation is a distinct permitted context, not a required retained-value observation.
pending.listed-no-double-colon-form: PENDING the otherwise identical complete SAVE kept form. Preserve the required token separation and exactly one explicit SAVE route. It is a standalone statement occurrence, not INTEGER,SAVE substituted as grammar evidence.
pending.omitted-list-form: PENDING a complete ordinary subroutine with separately typed local objects and exactly one bare SAVE. C893 excludes other explicit SAVE statements/attr-specs in that scope. Do not use bare SAVE in BLOCK: C1108 requires a list there. Admission is a compile positive control, not an empty runtime retention test.
pending.separator-without-list-exclusion: PENDING a complete otherwise valid local-variable context with SAVE :: but no saved entity list; repair only by removing :: or inserting the already declared kept with token separation. Pick one complete canonical pair rather than duplicate both repairs. Qualify the actual incomplete list-bearing form at its live source, including a justified parser terminator point only if measured; generic EOF, missing END or unsupported SAVE alone cannot supply the cause.
pending.mixed-list-and-separators: PENDING one complete ordinary subroutine declaring two local INTEGER variables, an eligible local PROCEDURE(interface),POINTER entity and a named COMMON block with a separate typed member. SAVE may list the variables, procedure pointer and /block_name/ once each. R401 owns comma expansion; missing/trailing-comma contrasts need a single punctuation repair, unchanged declarations and exact causes. COMMON members are not individually listed. Keep the complete abstract interface and8.5.16p4's other-scope obligations explicit.
pending.blanket-eligibility-and-scope-source: PENDING finite source relations to p1/C861/C862/C814 and C1108. Bare SAVE applies only to allowed same-scope items, not an automatic CHARACTER(len=n) local, dummy, result, named constant or individual COMMON member. Existing C814_valid__automatic_save_bare_save is a complete compile/positive-control candidate, not new execution. An outer SAVE does not save an independently declared BLOCK local; listed SAVE in BLOCK and object-name shadowing under19.5.1.4p2 require their own complete scopes. Do not apply the object-name rule blindly to the separate procedure-pointer/common-block alternatives.
pending.initialization-and-implicit-save-source: PENDING canonical source relations distinguishing explicit variable initialization or DATA under8.4p3, procedure-pointer initialization under15.4.3.6p6, BIND on a COMMON block under8.5.5p3, and main/module/submodule declarations under8.5.16p4. These implicit attributes are not extra textual SAVE statements. Component default initialization under7.5.4.6p6 does not imply SAVE of the containing object. Existing owners and all actual runtime/control roles remain unchanged.
pending.canonical-retention-and-occurrence-sourc: PENDING separately adjudicated whole-program/occurrence relations, not new local S effects. C815_valid contains an actual SAVE :: a statement in its mixed-attribute runtime; the C815 save-statement repair deletes that statement and retains only the type-declaration SAVE, so its filename is not statement evidence. The S8.5.16-001 RETURN/active-recursion parents likewise use type-declaration SAVE and retain their owners. S8.5.5-002 explicit confirmation has real SAVE /saved_pair/ occurrences but remains a run/positive-control. No cloning, role opt-in or automatic numbered-wrapper link is authorized. Unsaved reentry data cannot be read as a negative oracle, and saved association does not extend a dead target or internal-procedure host lifetime.

requirements.oracle: Complete statement-form compile admissions and one-defect minimally repaired syntax contrasts. The optional group and nonempty list come from original grammar, not processor consensus. The normative attribute-definition route and finite canonical reuse plans retain their source, occurrence, program, role and state prerequisites.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Reporting capability does not mandate fatal rejection, printed R859 or fixed English. A future exact diagnostic may be qualified by its complete source/control context rather than one preferred wording; echoes, unrelated origins, unqualified recovery, unsupported facilities and native/internal/resource failures do not establish the intended condition. SAVE preserves specified states but does not initialize them, allocate storage or authorize undefined-value/association inquiries. No whole-standard, runtime, ABI, source-use or approval credit follows from this source catalogue.

requirements.title: A saved entity is an object name, procedure-pointer name or named common block
requirements.definition: The three alternatives are object-name, proc-pointer-name and a common-block-name enclosed by two slashes. Explicit R804/C810 and R861/C894 govern the first two names; the complete502-rule head census finds no explicit common-block-name production, so R402 supplies its name convention and COMMON/scope rules supply identity. There is no array/coarray declarator group or unnamed common-block alternative in R860.

pending.ordinary-variable-name: PENDING a separately declared local INTEGER variable in a complete ordinary subroutine, named once in SAVE. Data-object name grammar is R804/C810, while variable eligibility is C861/C862. Do not use a named constant, dummy, function result, automatic object or COMMON member as this positive control.
pending.procedure-pointer-name: PENDING a complete ABSTRACT INTERFACE followed by a local PROCEDURE(interface),POINTER declaration and one SAVE callback statement. No pointer initializer, association, call or payload is needed for compile admission. R861/C894, C855 and15.4.3.6 own the naming/interface role. Share any future complete case with its canonical grammar owners only through an implemented, separately reviewed relationship.
pending.named-common-block: PENDING a complete ordinary subroutine with INTEGER :: member, COMMON /packet_block/ member, and SAVE /packet_block/. The block is one entity regardless of member count. For whole-program contexts, all other nonexempt declaring scopes must meet8.5.16p4 and matching COMMON storage/type rules. The member is not itself given SAVE explicitly; no binary layout or retained-value claim is supplied.
pending.required-common-block-name: PENDING a complete named-block source using SAVE // as the sole defect, repaired only by inserting the already declared packet_block between the slashes. R860 requires a name even though COMMON can spell blank common. Do not create an independent blank COMMON declaration, conflate blank-common persistence with SAVE, or accept an unrelated COMMON warning as the missing-name report.
pending.paired-common-delimiters: PENDING the same complete named-block source with one missing closing slash in SAVE /packet_block, repaired only by inserting it. Preserve block/member declarations and names. Deleting both slashes is not an equivalent negative: a bare common-name homonym can instead designate a local data object under19.3.2.
pending.whole-name-not-designator: PENDING a complete constant-bound local INTEGER array and SAVE a(1), repaired by deleting only (1) so the whole eligible array is saved. This grammar has no array-element/section or component designator alternative. Procedure invocation and component-specific variants require their own resolved role-valid repairs; no invalid scalar/automatic/COMMON-member control is substituted.
pending.entity-eligibility-and-identity-source: PENDING C861/C862/C814 and19.3.2 relations separating named block, member, variable, procedure pointer and ordinary procedure roles. A legal COMMON homonym can denote different entities in /name/ and bare-name contexts. Explicit SAVE confirmation of implicit SAVE differs from a second explicit specification under C815. Existing BIND COMMON effect/confirmation and C815 records retain actual complete sources, facets, phases and roles; no new connection or copied program is created.

requirements.oracle: Resolve each actual saved-entity spelling to its declared role before evaluating grammar or diagnostics. Finite compile admissions and delimiter/name/designator repairs use complete otherwise eligible contexts; COMMON and procedure-pointer sources are not inferred from tokens alone.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The lexical name conventions do not establish SAVE eligibility or lifetime. A named constant can be a data object but is excluded by C861; ordinary procedures cannot be relabelled procedure pointers. COMMON storage, obsolescence/reporting modes, program-wide declarations and pointer status remain distinct gates. No no-op effect, undefined reentry read or automatic canonical link is introduced.

requirements.title: A procedure-pointer name is an explicit name production
requirements.definition: proc-pointer-name is name. This explicit production, confirmed by the complete original grammar-head census, takes precedence over an assumed R402 expansion. R603/C601 define name spelling and C894 defines the required procedure-pointer identity; a valid name alone does not supply that identity.

pending.name-production-source: PENDING an exact finite source relation R861 -> R603/C601 with a fully declared local procedure pointer and complete interface under C894. Bind the actual SAVE name occurrence and its declaration. Reuse the one complete R860/C894 admission candidate only after independent source/role/relationship adjudication; no empty spelling classifier, fabricated long-name test or duplicate executable is required.
pending.name-not-invocation-source: PENDING a complete local procedure-pointer context whose SAVE callback() spelling is repaired only by deleting (). SAVE takes the name, not a procedure reference. The control uses the same declared procedure pointer and interface, with no invocation or dependence on association status. Select one canonical syntax owner with R860 rather than duplicating the same contrast or forcing a printed R861.

requirements.oracle: Original lexical grammar plus an actual declared procedure-pointer context and occurrence. Whole-name admission and source-minimal invocation-suffix removal remain pending canonical relations or compile controls, not new procedure-pointer effects.
requirements.oracle_limitation: A component reference, ordinary procedure, function result or undefined procedure-pointer invocation is not made eligible by the spelling of its name. Current supplementary-target link infrastructure does not automatically implement numbered-wrapper reuse. No source/case/relation approval is granted by this definition.

requirements.title: An omitted-list SAVE excludes other explicit SAVE appearances in its scope
requirements.definition: If a SAVE statement with no saved entity list appears in a scoping unit, no other appearance of a SAVE attr-spec or SAVE statement is permitted in that same scoping unit. This includes another bare or listed SAVE and the type-declaration SAVE route. It is a scope-wide syntactic restriction, not a last-statement-wins rule, a ban on implicit SAVE or a file-wide count.

pending.two-omitted-list-statements: PENDING a complete ordinary subroutine with separately typed local variables and two bare SAVE statements. Delete only one statement for the control. The actual second scope-wide SAVE appearance must be reported, not an EOF, missing declaration or unsupported keyword. The overlap with C815's explicit-attribute rule remains documented rather than manufacturing a second identical case.
pending.bare-and-listed-statements: PENDING both source orders, bare SAVE plus SAVE :: kept and the reverse, on an eligible local INTEGER kept. Delete the listed statement for the control without changing declarations or data. The presence of a list on the second statement does not bypass C893. Keep C815 overlap/cause attribution explicit and do not use a different invalid entity role to isolate the rule.
pending.bare-and-type-attribute: PENDING INTEGER,SAVE :: kept plus a bare SAVE in both otherwise legal specification orders, repaired by deleting only ,SAVE from the type declaration. There is no initializer or DATA statement in the initial family. The named attr-spec route and the omitted-list statement share the actual scoping unit; calibration must preserve the scope-wide condition and any C815 overlap.
pending.listed-only-controls: PENDING a complete scope with two different eligible locals, each named once in separate listed SAVE statements, and no bare SAVE. The C893 antecedent is false, but C815 still forbids repeating SAVE for the same entity. These are compile positive controls, not an assertion that any number of duplicate entity specifications is permitted.
pending.implicit-save-not-extra-syntax: PENDING source-qualified controls combining one bare SAVE with explicit initialization of a local variable, a separately valid DATA initialization, or another canonical implicit-SAVE route that contains no second SAVE token.8.4p3,15.4.3.6p6,8.5.5p3 and8.5.16p4 retain their own conditions. Component default initialization neither adds a SAVE statement nor itself implies SAVE of an ordinary containing local.
pending.separate-scope-and-BLOCK-boundaries: PENDING complete ordinary external/internal subprogram controls in different scoping units, each with its own local declaration and one bare SAVE.3.120 excludes nested scoping units. For BLOCK, C1108 independently prohibits an omitted list; use a valid listed local-variable SAVE control instead of treating inner bare SAVE as an admitted scope-separation example. Outer SAVE does not cover independently declared BLOCK locals.
pending.procedure-attribute-source-boundary: PENDING exact C893/C815/15.4.3.6 analysis before classifying a bare SAVE alongside a procedure-declaration SAVE proc-attr-spec. R1514 names that grammar category separately from R802 attr-spec; do not silently invent either an exemption or a uniquely C893 diagnostic. The local procedure pointer is SAVE-eligible, and repeated explicit attributes still retain C815. Implicit SAVE from pointer initialization is a different route. No generic procedure or missing interface supplies a valid control.

requirements.oracle: Complete same-scope statement/attribute matrices with one-deletion controls, distinct local identities and explicit overlap analysis. Count actual SAVE routes, not tokens in other scopes, comments, DATA values or an initializer's implied attribute.
requirements.oracle_limitation: The numbered reporting duty is not an unconditional fatal-exit, English-wording or code-printing requirement. A future complete message must be qualified with the exact forbidden source condition and legitimate staged origin; a coincident C815 or entity-eligibility report cannot silently establish every overlapping owner. No synthetic approval or blanket weakening of C893 is proposed.

requirements.title: A proc-pointer-name identifies an actual procedure pointer
requirements.definition: A proc-pointer-name denotes a procedure pointer. Naming an ordinary external, module, internal or dummy procedure does not give it the POINTER attribute. The separate object-name alternative in R860 remains valid for eligible data variables; the name's resolved role matters, not an arbitrary choice to parse all SAVE names as procedure pointers.

pending.local-procedure-pointer-admission: PENDING a complete ordinary subroutine with a complete non-elemental abstract subroutine interface, PROCEDURE(iface),POINTER :: callback, and SAVE callback. No initializer, call or association inquiry is required. C855/15.4.3.6 supplies EXTERNAL/interface conditions, while local rather than dummy/result identity satisfies C862.
pending.ordinary-procedure-exclusion: PENDING the same complete interface context with PROCEDURE(iface) :: callback lacking POINTER, repaired only by inserting ,POINTER in that declaration. Supply a matching complete external definition if the negative uses an ordinary external procedure identity; no link or call is used as the cause. C861's SAVE entity restriction overlaps C894, so select one canonical negative family and retain independently reviewed source relations rather than duplicate or overclaim the diagnostic.
pending.data-object-alternative-boundary: PENDING a correctly typed ordinary local INTEGER variable named in SAVE as a source/control relation to R860's object-name branch. Such a source is not a C894 negative because it is not attempting to denote a procedure pointer. Existing data-variable SAVE statements retain their primary owners and roles.
pending.dummy-result-interface-and-lifetime-sour: PENDING canonical C862 and procedure/pointer-state relations for procedure-pointer dummies/results and host-associated procedure names. Explicit local declarations establish identity; no unqualified host re-attribution is inferred from R861. Saving a pointer or sharing it across active recursive instances does not preserve an ended internal procedure's host instance or a dead data target. Any future call/association inquiry must first prove defined association, a live target and compatible complete interfaces. No undefined-pointer trap/value oracle or new local runtime facet is created.

requirements.oracle: Actual procedure-pointer declarations, complete interfaces and a one-attribute role repair, with C861/C862 and lexical R861 kept distinct. A mere name match or a procedure declaration without POINTER is not a sufficient premise.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Data-pointer and procedure-pointer roles, ordinary procedures and function results are different. Undefined association is not queried, SAVE is not a host/target lifetime extension, and success of a no-op compile does not supply retained association or invocation evidence. All future source/program/role/diagnostic gates require independent adjudication.

review_rationale: Independent complete original SAVE statement, pending-plan and finite existing-occurrence review1f30d1ea3c5736ee25250b6a2903975844a2ac47aa7c68e77cb3464ddc69e04c, registered in doc/source_audits/batch_078.json. R859 allows bare SAVE but its nested optional separator does not allow SAVE:: without a list. R860/R861 distinguish explicit R804 data names, explicit R861 procedure-pointer names and assumed R402 slash-delimited named COMMON; block/member/homonym identities remain exact. C893 is same-scope and antecedent-conditioned; implicit SAVE is not another textual appearance, while the R1514 proc-attr-spec versus R802 attr-spec overlap remains pending source qualification. C894 needs an actual eligible local procedure pointer with complete interface and C861/C862 conditions. P1's all items means allowed items in the same scoping unit; C814 and BLOCK C1108 retain automatic/dummy/result/member exclusions and list/no-COMMON conditions. Initialization, default-component initialization, module/main/submodule and BIND COMMON retain separate SAVE owners. Eight complete existing inputs were independently checked without retagging or new links: C815's repair and both local SAVE effect programs have no standalone SAVE, and BIND COMMON explicit confirmation has two occurrences but remains a positive control. All28facets stay pending. Retained state is not initialization or extended target/host lifetime.
